_comment: Two entries the sweep HELD were added by an agent pass under the per-entry sheet-check method described in docs/OPERATIONS.md. Each entry below carries its own measurement. Every one-sheet locality was left held; see _comment2.

SIGEL -> EVERGREEN: 8 reads, locality 107 m over 6 sheets against Green St 1422 m. All 69 attributed numerals (200-459) fall inside Martin's 200 to 499W. The sweep held it only because the losing candidate has no documented range to fall outside of.

VEDDER -> SCOTT: locality 117 m over 4 sheets, sole candidate, 12 numerals 619-669 inside Martin's 500 to 799W. The sweep's per-side guard fired on an artifact: three reads are W. VEDDER on a horizontal label and the fourth, on p52, is a wrapped near-square label at the sheet edge mis-prefixed N. VEDDER AV. -- p52's W. HEIN PL. carries the same wrapped shape and is unambiguously east-west. Martin documents exactly one Vedder St, and Scott St is east-west, so no per-side rename exists to express.

TOWNSEND, MILTON, W HEIN PL and CARL are each read on a sheet that also reads their modern value -- the pattern the _019 HAMILTON CT test treats as a refutation. None is one here. Georeferenced through each sheet's own GCPs, the historic labels land on the value's centerline: TOWNSEND 0-5 m over five placed sheets, W HEIN PL 0-5 m, CARL 1-2 m on p29/p30, MILTON 0-5 m on p46/p51. The sheets label one street twice, historic and modern, at opposite ends of its run rather than side by side. Two caveats kept on the record: MILTON's p36 and p40 labels land 33 and 30 m off, and CARL's p71 label 43 m off, all outside the 20 m bar -- so the on-street evidence is 2 of 4 sheets for MILTON and 2 of 3 for CARL, and both entries rest on their locality medians (53 m over 5 sheets, 105 m over 2) as much as on this.
